Cup Fraction Calculator

0.66 cups is ⅔ cup, or 10 tablespoons + 2 teaspoons. 0.33 cups is ⅓ cup (5 tbsp + 1 tsp), and 0.75 is ¾ cup (12 tbsp).

—

For baking, weighing in grams is more accurate. The cups to grams converter does the weights.

How it works

Type an amount like 0.66, 2/3 or 1 1/2. If it’s within 2% of a real measuring-cup size, it snaps to that size, so 0.33 becomes ⅓ cup and 0.66 becomes ⅔ cup. Otherwise it uses the biggest measuring cup that fits and makes up the rest with tablespoons and teaspoons, rounded to the nearest ⅛ teaspoon. It also shows the same amount in spoons only, for small amounts or a missing cup. It all runs in your browser. Nothing you type is sent anywhere or saved.

Ways to use it

  • A scaled recipe. The scaler says 0.66 cups; this says ⅔ cup.
  • Halving a recipe. Half of ¾ cup is ⅜ cup, or ¼ cup + 2 tbsp.
  • Metric recipes. Convert milliliters to cups first, then here.
  • Spoon amounts. When the right measuring cup is in the dishwasher.

Questions

Why not just use decimals?

Measuring cups are marked in fractions, not decimals. 0.66 cups is a number on a screen; ⅔ cup is a cup in your drawer.

How accurate is the rounding?

Amounts within 2% of a standard cup size snap to it. Anything else is measured out to the nearest ⅛ teaspoon, which is closer than most measuring cups are filled.

What is ⅔ cup in tablespoons?

⅔ cup is 10 tablespoons plus 2 teaspoons. ⅓ cup is 5 tablespoons plus 1 teaspoon.

Should I weigh instead?

For baking, yes. A cup of flour can weigh anywhere from 120 to 150 g depending on how it’s scooped. Weighing in grams takes that out of the equation.

Is anything saved?

No. The calculator runs in your browser and nothing is saved or sent anywhere.
